subject: physics
question_text: Give one example of how nanotechnology is used in modern technology.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 6 (printed p.143). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: targeted drug delivery is the standard example of nanotechnology in medicine, and that healthy tissue receiving far less drug is the correct benefit of a targeted release mechanism.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The example
lines: Targeted drug delivery is one example.
steps.why: Nanoparticles are small enough to travel through blood vessels and reach a tumour directly, a size only nanotechnology gives access to.
common_mistakes: Naming a broad field such as electronics instead of one specific example.
Leaving out that nanoparticles carry the drug, not an ordinary injection.
steps.memory_tip: One example: nanoparticles deliver the drug straight to the tumour.
steps.margin_note: Any correctly explained nanotechnology example is accepted.

steps.label: How it helps

lines.text: The drug releases only at the tumour.

lines: Healthy tissue receives far less of the drug
steps.why: Releasing the drug only where it is needed reduces the amount that reaches healthy cells, which is the main benefit nanotechnology adds here.
common_mistakes: Describing the nanoparticle instead of stating the benefit it gives.
Confusing targeted drug delivery with a vaccine or an antibiotic.
steps.memory_tip: Less drug reaches healthy tissue: that is the benefit line to write.
steps.margin_note: State the benefit in one sentence, not the chemistry of the particle.
